title: CLISubject
description: Canonical identity of a command-line invocation as a first-class subject, coexisting with package subjects (purl) without impersonating one. Identity is tool + version + structural command path + semantic options + operand classes + OS/arch + shell/runtime. Execution outcome (exit code, termination, stream fingerprints, timestamps) is evidence about the subject (cli-execution-evidence.json), never part of it. Literal option values, operands, paths, hosts and credentials never enter: each is reduced to a closed value class. The reference form is cli:<tool>[@<version>][/<path segment>...]?opt=<name>[:<class>]&operand=<class>&os=&arch=&shell=&runtime=.

tool.description: Lowercased executable name without directory or launcher suffix (.exe, .cmd, .bat, .ps1).

toolVersion.description: The tool's own reported version, probed before the run.

path.description: Command path below the tool, one segment per word: gh workflow run is ["workflow","run"]. Absent for tools with no subcommand vocabulary.

options.description: Semantic flags sorted by name and deduplicated; order is not identity. valueClass is present only when the sanitizer knows the flag takes a value.

operands.description: Positional argument classes in the order given; order is identity.

shell.description: The shell that launched the tool: bash, zsh, pwsh, powershell, cmd, or direct.

runtime.description: The runtime the tool executes inside, only for tools bound to one: "node 22.18" for npx, "go 1.26.5" for go test.

valueClass.description: What a literal became. A secret's class records that the option took a credential; the credential itself is never recorded.
